newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cie Bancaire sees 1.2 bln Ffr 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Cie Bancaire sees 1.2 bln Ffr 1996 loss.

text.p: Compagnie Bancaire, a unit of Groupe Paribas, forecast on Tuesday a 1996 net consolidated loss of 1.2 billion francs after taking 2.5 billion francs in property provisions.

"The consequences of different decisions taken by the group mean it will be in loss for 1996. The consolidated net attributable loss will be 1.2 billion francs," it said. It said it would maintain its 1996 net dividend at 10 francs.
The bank also said it reaped a capital gain of about one billion francs on sale of a six percent stake in its consumer credit arm Cetelem.
Money from the sale would go toward the property provisions.
Compagnie Bancaire reported profits of 602 million francs for 1995.
Compagnie Bancaire said that the provisions would allow it to "exit from the property crisis" which has weighed on its performance for several years.
"Since 1991, the weight on its accounts of charges resulting from the property crisis has masked the growth in profits of others sectors of the group," it said.
To help its recovery, Compagnie Bancaire said it had "chosen to integrate into its accounts from 1996, the consequences of the acceleration of its disengagement from property risks."
It said that the provisions would cover the property exposure of its units Sinvim and UCB.
It said the provisions should allow in particular UCB and its subsidiaries to reach breakeven as of 1997.
